turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: China's power has peaked because its rise now meets stronger resistance at home and abroad. Its economy, technology, and influence still matter, but each faces limits that were weaker during its rapid ascent. A plateau is still power, but it is no longer a climb.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: CON

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: The key question is direction, not perfection. China still adds tools and relationships, so calling its power peaked mistakes slower growth for a final limit.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Your weakest point is treating any new relationship as added power. A connection matters only if China can turn it into lasting influence, and fragile dependence does not prove that.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: China's power never determines outcomes by itself. Every serious contest depends on choices by other states, so no single peak can describe China's total power or its future direction.

turns.text: Because adaptation does not prove decline; it proves others are limiting China. New tools cannot erase demographic strain and resistance, so China's overall power has peaked despite local wins.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Consider a country that once copied China's infrastructure model but now seeks Chinese finance and technology on stricter terms. That is deeper, negotiated influence, showing China's power still grows.
